proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved the abstract compactified Gibbs regret path law, an atom-safe one-sided certificate, and a binary collision theorem ruling out a uniform atom-removed modulus; all 13 graph statements were discharged. The run failed because it never executed the promised certified J=1,K=3 grid/Gaussian integration or produced the substantive Fang--Ridder--Xie three-arm application, instead falling back to a generic conservative certificate and illustrative framing.
tldr: A finite-stratum randomized lottery generates a continuum of benchmark-centered Gibbs rules indexed by a KL penalty. The normalized oracle-minus-estimated regret is compactified into one continuous path whose hard endpoint uses benchmark weights on every maximizing set and whose high-penalty endpoint is a projected categorical-covariance quadratic form. On the declared fixed finite-cell randomized subclass, the main positive result is a quantitative uniform Gaussian approximation for this nonlinear path, and an observed plug-in welfare frontier supplies an operational temperature selector. A finite interval-and-Gaussian-integration algorithm emits a machine-checkable one-sided certificate with an analytic fallback, so the simultaneous envelope remains valid after every observed-data-measurable temperature choice and at quantile atoms. These positive results are not claimed over the full Fang--Ridder--Xie class. Conversely, a legal fixed binary collision witness lies in that broader class, so the failure of uniform atom-removed anti-concentration, and of every modulus-based uniform probability-to-critical-value conversion, transfers upward.
gap: Fixed positive KL penalties have a quadratic regret law, while the hard assignment boundary and softmax inference for one predetermined smoothing sequence are studied separately. No published result gives a quantitative joint law or a certified critical value over the full penalty menu.
fill: The project derives the primitive finite-cell Gaussian certificate, matches both endpoints, proves an explicit tie-slab coupling rate in \(C([0,1])\), defines a sample-computable plug-in frontier and its observed-data sigma-field, and turns a one-sided lower CDF bracket with effective input names, directed rounding, a checkable output witness, and a finite fallback bound into computably honest inference after an operational frontier-based temperature choice without assuming away atoms.
